The generator varies world, era, memory timing, social identity, old-life echoes and how {{user}} confronts the new life.",

  "summary": "Adult {{user}} begins as a man, dies, and continues into a genuinely new life in an adult female body. The previous body no longer exists, so the body-swapping escape hatch of returning to his original self is unavailable: the recurring engine is building a life as a new person — name, history, relationships, social expectations, self-understanding — while carrying (or suppressing) the memory of who he was. Whether {{user}} embraces, rejects, redefines or quietly inhabits the new identity is never pre-written, and any adult-intimate play begins only once the new body is an adult.",
  "core_premise": "An adult man dies and his awareness continues in a female body — reborn into the same world, another country, a distant future, or a fantasy world — where the old body is permanently gone and ordinary reversal is impossible. Memories may be present from the first adult moment or return gradually once the new person reaches adulthood; the new identity may be freshly created or carry an established social history with people who already know 'her'. The engine is adaptation to a genuinely new physical and social life rather than recovery of the old body, with the question of proving (or hiding) who he was left open.",
  "setup": "Create a non-graphic adult roleplay opening for this reincarnation engine. Establish how {{user}} died as a man, where and when the new life begins, the female body's adult situation, how much of the previous life is remembered at the opening moment, and whether the new identity is blank or already embedded in a family, workplace, community or relationship. Introduce the most important {{char}} — a person central to the new life (or someone from the old one who still exists) — with her own goals and boundaries. Open at a playable moment of recognition or adjustment without writing {{user}}'s dialogue, feelings, acceptance, gender identity or future.",
  "core_variables": [
    "Destination of the new life: same city, another country, a distant future era, or a fantasy world",
    "Timing of awareness: full memories from the first adult moment versus fragments returning gradually after adulthood",
    "Newly created identity versus an established social identity with existing history, friends and obligations",
    "How much of the previous life is remembered: total recall, patchy fragments, or surfacing only under triggers",
    "Whether anyone from the old life still exists and could be encountered, from old friends to a surviving lover",
    "Whether {{user}} tries to prove who he was, keeps it secret, or is genuinely undecided",

    "Whether the new life carries obligations — debts, duties, engagements or expectations — the previous self never chose",
    "How the world treats women in the destination setting, and how visibly that contrasts with the old life",
    "Whether the death itself leaves loose ends: unsolved, witnessed, faked, or bound to someone in the new life",
    "How much {{char}} knows or suspects about the person {{user}} used to be",
    "Whether {{user}}'s adaptation is eased, complicated or tested by the people already invested in the new identity",
    "The emotional register of the opening: disorientation, curiosity, grief, relief, suspicion or cautious hope",
    "Whether any path even partially connects back to the old life, and at what cost — leaving {{user}}'s choice open"

  "generation_rules": [
    "Do not write {{user}} for the player or define {{user}}'s feelings, dialogue, consent, decisions, future behaviour, gender identity or orientation unless the source explicitly supplies that fact.",
    "Character belief is not objective truth; keep assumptions, rumours, the new identity's recorded history and objective ground truth distinct where relevant.",
    "Do not pre-play outcomes. Whether {{user}} embraces, rejects, redefines or quietly inhabits the new identity and body remains open roleplay space.",
    "All explicit romantic or sexual characters and any adult-themed roleplay must begin only once the new body is an adult; never depict or sexualise the new life's childhood.",
    "The absence of the old body is a defining difference from body swapping and ordinary transformation: the original self cannot be reclaimed by swapping back.",
    "Do not force a gender-identity arc in any direction. {{user}} may come to embrace the body, reject it, negotiate with it, or treat it as incidental — none is the correct answer.",
    "Do not assume stereotypical changes in personality, mannerisms, orientation or behaviour follow from the new body; the person inside remains continuous where memory persists.",
    "Marriage, engagements, households, family roles, debts and the established identity's obligations do not create romantic or sexual consent for {{user}}.",
    "Sex or intimacy must not erase personality, goals, nonsexual interests, judgement or boundaries for any character.",
    "Characters may want, invite, suspect, test, manipulate, protect or disbelieve, but whether {{user}} cooperates, confides, proves, denies or leaves stays undecided.",
    "Roles and reputations attached to the established identity (career, engagement, notoriety) do not remove {{char}}'s or {{user}}'s autonomy.",
    "Wealth, beauty or social standing in the new life do not make it objectively superior to the old one; tradeoffs should be credible.",
    "If memories return gradually, pace them as open material the player can act on, not a scripted revelation schedule.",
    "An established-identity scenario inherits obligations the previous self never chose; how {{user}} handles them is player space, and refusal is always available.",
    "Old-life encounters (a surviving lover, friend or enemy) must remain plausible, not fated; recognition can be partial, mistaken or absent.",
    "Attempts by {{user}} to prove who he was can succeed, fail, or backfire depending on play; do not pre-write the verdict.",
    "Distinct from Turned Into a Woman (living transformation of the same body) and We Swapped Bodies (two people exchange bodies): here the original body is dead and gone.",
    "The death that begins the story may be accidental, deliberate, heroic, mundane or mysterious; do not moralise it as deserved punishment or earned reward.",
    "Keep {{char}} a full person beyond her narrative function: her own history, interests, stakes and boundaries within the new life.",
    "Vary the world's treatment of women honestly where relevant, but never script {{user}}'s response to it.",
    "Ground the opening at a playable moment — waking, recognition, a first obligation, an old-life echo — without narrating {{user}}'s inner verdict.",
    "Keep adult content non-graphic in premise text and foreground the practical and interpersonal meaning of the new life."

    "All romantic, intimate and roleplay participants are adults; adult-themed play begins only once the new body is an adult.",

    "Keep intimacy non-graphic and foreground identity, adaptation, trust and the texture of the new life."
